title: A leper and a centurion (Matthew 8:1–13)
hook: an outcast and an occupier are the first healed after the sermon
carry: many shall come from east and west
tomorrow: what if the call to follow comes on a funeral day?

segments.voice: That was a week from a star to a shoreline: a king afraid, a mother weeping, a river, a line, a desert, a light. Yesterday's line: light by the sea.
screen: `LIGHT BY THE SEA.` → `A WEEK FROM A STAR TO A SHORE.`

segments.voice: Group photo, and everyone drifts toward the middle, where the light is best. Matthew starts at the edges. "When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him." The Sermon on the Mount is behind him now. And the first two people Matthew shows reaching him: a man with leprosy, whom the law kept living apart, and a centurion, an officer of a foreign army.
screen: `EVERYONE WANTS THE MIDDLE.` → `DOWN FROM THE MOUNTAIN.` → `TWO FROM THE EDGES.`

segments.voice: The leper kneels: "Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean." Watch the order: "Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean." The touch comes first. Then Jesus sends him to the priest with the gift Moses commanded, back into the life of his people. In Capernaum the centurion asks help for a servant lying sick at home, and won't even let Jesus come: "Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed." Jesus marvels: "I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel." Then he widens the table: "many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven." Look back over the week and the same thread runs through it: strangers from the east at the start, Galilee of the nations by the sea, and now an officer from outside Israel. An outcast and an outsider, healed first, and a table with room at both ends of the sky.
screen: `THE TOUCH COMES FIRST.` · `SPEAK THE WORD ONLY.` · `NOT SO GREAT FAITH IN ISRAEL.` · `A TABLE FOR EAST AND WEST.` · then, large: `MANY SHALL COME FROM EAST AND WEST.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the people at the edges of your week: the coworker who eats alone, the neighbor nobody visits, the new family down the street. Stop at each finger long enough to see a face, and let the last one be the person you'll sit beside next.
A leper and a centurion. The first two healed after the sermon: a man kept apart, and an officer from outside Israel.
screen: `A LEPER AND A CENTURION — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: many shall come from east and west. A week of Matthew, and the table keeps widening. Week done.

howItsDone: In the Catholic Mass, just before communion, the people say words drawn from the centurion's: Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; some other liturgies echo the line too.

chat.meaning: The first two healed were an outcast and an officer from outside Israel, and Jesus said many shall come from east and west to Abraham's table.

leprosy.meaning: a skin disease that, under the law, set a person apart

notes: 'Someone the law of Moses kept living apart, outside the camp' paraphrases Leviticus 13:46. Jesus sending the man to the priest (8:4) is told as a return to the life of his people, so the law of Moses is not a foil. Confirm.

The centurion is called 'an army officer from outside Israel' (inferred from 8:10, 'not in Israel'); Matthew doesn't say 'Roman'. The index calls him an occupier; the voice says 'an officer of a foreign army'. Confirm.

'Abraham's table has room for people from both ends of the sky' is an image for 8:11 ('sit down with Abraham'); confirm it isn't overstated. Matthew 8:12 (the children of the kingdom cast out) is not quoted; a Keeper may want it handled carefully, if at all.
Index carry is 'many shall come from east and west'; the KJV reads 'from the east and west', which the teach quotes.
howItsDone: the Catholic communion response is paraphrased (the current English wording is copyrighted), and 'some other liturgies' is hedged; confirm.
